ideas.title: The pineapple that breaks dessert.
ideas.targetAudience: Curious home cooks and dessert makers who use fruit in gelatin recipes.
ideas.whyWatch: A glossy pink gelatin mould visibly wobbles beneath a counterintuitive pineapple hook, then its illustrated protein support is cut and collapses.
ideas.visibleEvent: Original 3D gel geometry and camera move from frame 0. A scissors/protein-network metaphor progressively severs strands and collapses into a pool. A direct fresh-versus-canned ingredient scene delivers the recipe consequence.
ideas.payoff: Fresh pineapple can prevent gelatin setting because bromelain breaks down gelatin proteins; canning heat inactivates the enzyme. Follow the gelatin recipe’s fruit instructions.

variants.title: The pineapple that breaks dessert.
variants.caption:
Fresh pineapple can stop gelatin from setting. Its bromelain enzymes break down gelatin proteins; the heat used in canning inactivates them.
Making a gelatin dessert? Use the fruit your recipe calls for.
Original 3D and graphic illustration, not a kitchen test. Sources: UGA Extension; Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics.

media.altText: Glossy pink illustrated gelatin wobbles on a lilac plate. A bright pink protein-network metaphor is cut by yellow scissors, then collapses. Fresh pineapple is contrasted with canned pineapple: active bromelain versus heat-inactivated enzyme. Practical advice: choose canned pineapple for gelatin and follow the recipe’s fruit instructions.
